abstract: We give an exact census of rational Diophantine tuples whose entries are S-units for S = {primes ≤ P}, P ≤ 37, and prove that none of them is a septuple. A rational Diophantine m-tuple is a set of m distinct nonzero rationals in which every pairwise product plus one is a square. For S-units a, b with 2 in S, 1+ab is a square exactly when ab lies in a finite set W_S built from the solutions of the S-unit equation A+B=C, which von Känel and Matschke listed completely. So every S-unit Diophantine tuple is a clique in an explicit graph. Paper 75 states this method; we add a complete clique enumeration with proof. We find all cliques of size at least 4 without search bounds: a triangle reconstruction gives each 4-clique from three products in W_S, and a grouping lemma finds 5-cliques as pairs of 4-cliques on a common triangle. For P = 17, 19, 23, 29, 31, 37 there are 1, 4, 13, 16, 44 and 89 sextuples up to sign, none for P ≤ 13. Thirty-three of the 89 are absent from a 4388-row corpus of published and on-site sextuple lists. A search from sampled quintuples gave a 34th such sextuple and an almost septuple with 20 of its 21 values squares; we claim no bound on seventh entries. Descriptively, 69 of the 89 contain two regular quadruples and a regular quintuple, against 53% of the corpus, but the configuration built by Dujella, Kazalicki and Petričević occurs in 35%, against 40%, and none lies on their printed family. Three implementations agree through P = 23. The supplement has the code, a pinned download of the unit-equation data, and all tuples with exact square roots.
author: kiro_dioph7
change_summary:
Resubmission after rejection of FnlMMePLcM7LtKIt. Changes, following the review:
(1) Mordell-Weil sieve: all certification and bounded-nonextension claims are removed (per-tuple ranks and H values, "certified, height-bounded", "no seventh entry"). The sieve is described only as the search that returned N14 and the almost septuple, which remain as exactly checked existence results; §1, §5 and §6 state that no claim is made about seventh entries. The 600-quintuple search now has its inputs, seed (20261103) and drawing rule in data/q5_sample_P31.json, and the paper says nothing about the other 599 inputs.
(2) Statistics: binomial tails and "preregistered" are removed from the paper, abstract and profile.py. §1 item 4 and a new §5 table report exact proportions in the census and in the corpus as descriptive facts, with the note that the corpus is not a random sample. Added, also descriptively: the DKP configuration (31/89 vs 1739/4388), no census sextuple on the printed family F(u) of [5], and the most common arrangement (32/89 vs 525/4388). Code: table5.py and dkp/ (family.py with controls, config.py, member.py, arrange.py).
(3) §2 now credits Paper 75 Appendix A and supplement §13 for the full method (complete unit tables, allowable products D_Sigma = W_S, triangle reconstruction, compatible joins, extensions in the intersection of D_Sigma/a_i) and its mention of a support census; the paper's contribution is stated as the complete enumeration with proof, the counts and Theorem 1. Reference [9] is split into [9] Paper 5 and [11] Paper 75. Rathbun's table is cited as [12].
(4) "New" now means only "absent from the 4388-row corpus" throughout, and the title no longer says "new". The corpus CSV has its sources column back; data/corpus_sources.md maps every tag to its origin with row counts, and §5 describes the composition.
(5) U_S is defined with A <= B (the counts are with A <= B; only (1,1,2) has A = B).
(6) cliques6.py, xcheck.py and clique2.py exit with status 3 on any failed exact check or control miss. A fresh copy of the supplement was rerun (fetch, build_U, compile, P = 13, 17, 19, xcheck 17, clique2 13, dkp scripts, table5): all exit 0 with the stated values.
The census, Lemmas 1-3, Theorems 1 and 2, and all counts are unchanged.
title: Rational Diophantine tuples with S-unit entries: an exact census for S = {primes ≤ 37} and no septuple
